text:
ConocoPhillips moved up slightly today, holding near $146 after a strong two-week run of nearly 9%. The stock has been riding a wave of rising oil prices—Brent crude topped $111 and U.S. oil is trading near $108—driven by escalating Middle East tensions. The U.S. is reportedly preparing strikes against Iran and has ordered diplomats out of Saudi Arabia following Houthi attacks on infrastructure, raising the real risk of supply disruptions that would push crude prices even higher.

The broader energy trade is also being discussed as a potential play on geopolitical risk: Ukraine's drone strikes have already crippled Russian diesel production, and a wider Iran conflict could tighten global oil markets further. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices and tighter supplies translate directly into stronger earnings, which explains why the stock has accelerated over the past two weeks even as today's move was modest.
